[Find out more here](https://news.sap.com/2026/11/sap-expands-collaboration-astrazeneca-rise-with-sap-business-ai).

These articles reflect the diverse applications and implications of AI across various fields today.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.” [...] He urged others across the military to adopt his hands-on approach to AI integration, encouraging troops to partner with AI experts to learn cutting-edge techniques and to tap innovative service members as in-house AI gurus who can spread that knowledge further.

        Sign up for our daily newsletter so you never miss a beat on all things federal

items.title: From scans to scribes, Yale medical faculty talk AI use in healthcare | Yale Daily News
items.summary:
Normally, diagnosing prostate cancer includes a blood test, MRI imaging and a formal diagnosis from a radiologist, who might read the same MRI image differently on different days.

Now, Onofrey said, he and other researchers are training deep learning models on these images to look for diseases including prostate cancer, though he said researchers have not validated models in large enough settings for clinical adoption yet. [...] Technology companies will face skepticism, according to Papademetris. Many AI models remain “black box” models, meaning users do not know the details of the inner workings behind the AI used in practice.

Though scientific advancement is exciting, Papademetris cautioned about implementing AI into healthcare without the proper guardrails in place. [...] Some provider systems, such as Yale Health, have incorporated AI scribes to help draft notes from patient visits. Yale researchers and professors spoke to the News about their experiences with AI-powered tools. Xenophon Papademetris, a professor at the School of Medicine, said people should be skeptical of AI use in everyday clinical practice.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] In October, several states sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gives dangerous medical advice and misleads consumers about safety. OpenAI says it will continue to improve the model. [...] We are not proposing a new regulatory regime, which may not be needed. The insurance industry’s crash tests have spurred automakers to build safer vehicles, beyond what federal rules require. AI companies could publish behavioral test results, letting hospitals, health insurers, and consumers choose accordingly.

items.title: AstraZeneca to Adopt RISE with SAP and Business AI | SAP News Center
items.summary: This press release was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence and has been reviewed by the editorial team.This document contains forward-looking statements, which are predictions, projections, or other statements about future events. These statements are based on current expectations, forecasts, and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results and outcomes to materially differ. Additional information regarding these risks and [...] AstraZeneca is exploring a range of business AI capabilities from SAP, including the Industry AI portfolio, the Joule solution and agentic use cases across finance, supply chain and manufacturing. These capabilities have the potential to enhance productivity, strengthen data quality and governance, and enable faster decision-making. [...] “SAP has been a key part of how we run our operations for more than two decades,” Chris Taylor, Chief Information Officer, AstraZeneca, said. “This next chapter of our partnership is about much more than modernizing technology. Through Axial, we are simplifying how AstraZeneca operates and creating the foundations to move faster and unlock greater value from AI. That matters because the faster we can turn insight into action, the faster we can create value for our company and for patients.”
